title: Onboarding checklist content draft (Console + Docs) — rough step copy + acceptance criteria
content:
Context
- This is the working content draft for the in-Console “Guided onboarding / First production launch” checklist.
- Goal: reduce onboarding friction + reduce top support tickets by making required steps explicit and discoverable.
- This doc is intentionally rough. It will be normalized into:
  1) Console step list + step detail drawer copy
  2) Canonical docs page (checklist) + linked how-tos (per step)
  3) Event instrumentation acceptance (to compute progress)

Target audience (MVP)
- PLG/self-serve Hosted API developers (startup → mid-market).
- Secondary: enterprise evaluators who need “production readiness” framing for internal approvals.

Tone notes (Console copy)
- Short, action-oriented, no jargon.
- “Why it matters” should be 1 sentence max.
- Warnings are allowed but should be specific (e.g., “429 = quota/rate limit; add backoff”).

Checklist structure proposal
- Two sections:
  A) “Get to first success” (TTFS)
  B) “Get to first production launch” (TTFP)
- Each step:
  - name (short)
  - 1–2 lines of instructions
  - acceptance criteria (what counts as “complete”)
  - links: Console deep link + docs link + quickstart/example link


A) Get to first success (TTFS)

Step A1 — Create an API key
Draft step name (Console): Create an API key
Draft short copy: Create a key in the Console and store it securely. Keys are scoped to your org/project.
Why it matters (optional): You’ll need this key to authenticate every request.
Acceptance criteria:
- Key is created in Console (control plane).
- (Telemetry) Emit server-side event when key is created.
  - Proposed event: onboarding.api_key_created
  - Must include: org_id, project_id (if applicable), actor_type=user/admin, source=console
Links:
- Console deep link: Settings → API Keys
- Docs: API keys + env vars (redwood-docs/pr-926)
Support pitfalls to address:
- Copy should explicitly call out “Don’t include quotes when exporting to env var.”

Step A2 — Set environment variable / configure SDK
Draft step name: Set your API key in your environment
Draft short copy: Add REDWOOD_API_KEY to your environment (or configure your SDK client).
Acceptance criteria:
- Hard to prove directly; recommend treating as “soft” completion OR derived from first authenticated request.
- Option 1 (simpler): mark complete when we see first request with valid key (2xx).
- Option 2 (client hint): SDK emits onboarding.env_configured (but we’re avoiding client-side reliance per eventing ADR).
Notes:
- Might be merged into A3 (“Make a successful request”) to reduce “unverifiable” steps.
Links:
- Docs: API key + environment setup (pr-926)
- Quickstart: production readiness quickstart (pr-377)

Step A3 — Make your first successful request (2xx)
Draft step name: Make a successful API request
Draft short copy: Send a request that returns a 2xx response.
Acceptance criteria:
- First 2xx response from gateway for org_id.
- Event emission: onboarding.first_successful_request
- Define precisely what endpoints count (chat/generate/embeddings/rerank).
- Exclusions:
  - health endpoints
  - Console “test” calls? (open question)
Links:
- Quickstart: “Hello world” snippet (docs)
- Example: streaming chat example (pr-506) if we want to push streaming early; otherwise link to minimal snippet

Step A4 — (Optional but recommended) Try streaming
Draft step name: Try streaming responses
Draft short copy: Enable streaming to reduce time-to-first-token and improve UX.
Acceptance criteria:
- First request with streaming=true that successfully establishes stream.
- Event emission: onboarding.first_stream_established
Notes:
- Should include 1-liner on client handling (disconnects are common).
Links:
- Example: streaming chat prod-ready reference (pr-506)
- SDK guides: streaming reconnect patterns (ENG-5820)
Support pitfalls to address:
- “If the connection drops, retry with exponential backoff; don’t replay non-idempotent operations blindly.”


B) First production launch (TTFP)

Step B1 — Add timeouts + retries (production-safe defaults)
Draft step name: Add timeouts and retries
Draft short copy: Configure request timeouts and exponential backoff retries for transient failures.
Acceptance criteria:
- Prefer “doc-confirmed” acceptance (unverifiable) OR derived from SDK UA tag/preset usage.
- Possible telemetry:
  - SDK preset sets header: X-Redwood-Retry-Preset: standard
  - Gateway emits event when header is present: onboarding.retries_configured
Open question:
- Is it acceptable to rely on SDK hints for this step? ADR preference is server-side emission + limited client hints (ok if treated as hint, not source of truth).
Links:
- SDK production defaults doc (ENG-5820)
- SDK PRs:
  - Python presets (redwood-sdk-python/pr-1183)
  - TS snippet generator (redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-804)
  - Go streaming reconnect helper (redwood-sdk-go/pr-412)
Support pitfalls to address:
- Clarify what to do on 429 vs 5xx vs timeouts.

Step B2 — Understand rate limits and quotas
Draft step name: Review quotas and rate limits
Draft short copy: Check your quota, expected throughput, and how to handle 429s.
Acceptance criteria:
- Console visit to Quotas page is weak (page view ≠ understanding).
- Alternative: mark complete when user opens the step details and clicks “I understand” (but that’s a guided tour pattern; maybe not MVP).
- Proposed compromise: mark complete when:
  - user has either visited quotas page OR encountered a 429 and then visited quotas page (stronger signal)
  - event(s): onboarding.first_429_received + onboarding.quotas_viewed
Links:
- Console deep link: Usage/Quotas
- Docs: rate limits + recommended backoff (new/needs confirmation)
Support tickets it maps to:
- 429 surprise after launch (SUP-18510)

Step B3 — Set a budget / usage alert
Draft step name: Set a budget alert
Draft short copy: Add a budget to avoid surprises as traffic ramps.
Acceptance criteria:
- Budget created in Console OR via Terraform snippet.
- Event emission: onboarding.budget_alert_configured
Links:
- Terraform sample budget alerts (redwood-terraform/pr-233)
- Console deep link: Billing → Budgets (or Usage → Budgets; confirm IA)
Open questions:
- Do all tenants have access to budgets in MVP? If not, we need conditional steps.

Step B4 — Pin your model version
Draft step name: Pin a model version
Draft short copy: Pin a specific model/version to keep behavior stable across upgrades.
Acceptance criteria:
- A pinned model is set for the relevant project (control plane config).
- Event emission: onboarding.model_pinned
Notes:
- Copy should call out that unpinned “latest” can change.
Links:
- Console deep link: Models → (select) → Pin
- Docs: model versioning + rollouts (existing page? if not, create)

Step B5 — Configure a fallback policy
Draft step name: Set a fallback model
Draft short copy: Configure a fallback so your app stays up during capacity constraints or model issues.
Acceptance criteria:
- Fallback policy configured for the project/route.
- Event emission: onboarding.fallback_configured
Notes:
- For MVP, fallback may be limited (region/model variant). We should avoid promising too much.
Links:
- Console deep link: Routing/Policies (confirm actual nav)
- Docs: “Fallbacks and graceful degradation” (may need to be written)

Step B6 — Add basic observability hooks
Draft step name: Add request IDs and logging
Draft short copy: Log request IDs and latency so you can debug issues in production.
Acceptance criteria:
- Weakly measurable.
- Option: mark complete when we detect customer sending a client request header like X-Request-ID or using SDK logging hook (UA tag).
- Alternative: step is “Visit usage dashboard” (measurable) + doc encourages logging.
Links:
- Console deep link: Observability → Requests / Traces (if available)
- Docs: “Debugging requests (request_id)” (likely exists; confirm)
Support tickets it maps to:
- streaming disconnect confusion (SUP-18488) — logging helps

Step B7 — Verify usage dashboard and data latency expectations
Draft step name: Check your usage dashboard
Draft short copy: Confirm you can see requests and understand dashboard update delay.
Acceptance criteria:
- Console visit to Usage dashboard + at least one request in last N minutes.
- Event emission: onboarding.usage_dashboard_viewed
Copy requirements:
- Must explicitly mention that dashboard can lag by ~X minutes (need confirmed number) to prevent “requests not counted” confusion.
Support tickets it maps to:
- usage dashboard lag confusion (SUP-18544)

Step B8 — Send first production traffic
Draft step name: Send production traffic
Draft short copy: Route real production traffic and monitor errors/latency.
Acceptance criteria (TTFP definition input):
- First request with environment=prod OR first request from a production API key OR first sustained traffic threshold.
- We need a robust definition that doesn’t misclassify “curl test” as prod.
- Proposed metric: first hour with ≥ N requests from ≥ M distinct end users OR a configured “prod key” label.
- Telemetry options:
  - Allow customers to label API keys as “prod” in Console (then event onboarding.prod_key_labeled + first 2xx using that key).
  - Use SDK UA tag “prod” (but will be inconsistent).
Open question:
- Do we want “prod” to be customer-declared (simple, explicit) for MVP?
Links:
- Docs: “Going live checklist” (this page)


Step ordering and gating
- Keep to ~8–10 steps max in MVP to avoid overwhelm.
- Consider showing “recommended” vs “required” tags.
- Steps should be conditional:
  - Streaming step only if user uses chat/generate endpoints that support streaming.
  - Budgets only if plan supports budgets.
  - Fallback/pinning only if those Console features are enabled for the tenant.

Eventing notes (for Logan/Nadia)
- For each step we need:
  - server-side event name
  - idempotency key strategy (avoid step regressions from out-of-order events)
  - minimal payload (PII-free)
- Must align with onboarding-event-schema-v1 and ADR 2025-02.
- Known issue from dogfood: out-of-order event handling can regress checklist state (ENG-5866 / PR-28510).

Draft event name list (WIP)
- onboarding.api_key_created
- onboarding.first_successful_request
- onboarding.first_stream_established
- onboarding.first_429_received
- onboarding.quotas_viewed
- onboarding.budget_alert_configured
- onboarding.model_pinned
- onboarding.fallback_configured
- onboarding.usage_dashboard_viewed
- onboarding.prod_traffic_detected (or onboarding.first_prod_request)


Acceptance criteria rubric (how strict are we?)
- Strong (preferred): derived from server-side system state or gateway events (API key exists, 2xx observed, policy configured).
- Medium: derived from Console actions that imply progress (visited page + relevant state exists).
- Weak: self-attested or “clicked” completion.
- For MVP: avoid weak/self-attested unless there’s no alternative.

Open questions / unresolved
1) Do we keep A2 (env var) as a distinct step? It’s hard to verify and may be redundant with first 2xx.
2) TTFS definition: is it “first 2xx ever” or “first 2xx to a core endpoint (chat/generate/embeddings)”? Does embeddings count?
3) “Try streaming” — is streaming part of TTFS funnel or a “recommended” TTFS step?
4) TTFP definition: customer-declared “prod” (API key label) vs inferred sustained traffic.
5) How do we avoid penalizing multi-project orgs? Funnel should be tenant-level but allow per-project drilldown.
6) Console deep link ownership: need final URL/route IDs from Console team.
7) Budget step availability: confirm which plans have budgets and whether it’s in Console MVP.
8) Fallback policy scope: per-route vs per-project. What’s shipped for Hosted API today vs “coming soon”?
9) Copy constraints: how many characters fit in step list and step detail drawer? (Kenji/Tessa to confirm.)
10) Localization? Assume English-only MVP.

Notes from Support (to incorporate)
- 401/403: customers frequently set the wrong env var name or paste a key with whitespace.
- 429: customers treat as “platform down” and keep retrying aggressively; we must explicitly call out exponential backoff.
- Streaming disconnects: customers don’t realize they need reconnect logic; include a snippet link.
- Usage dashboard lag: call it out upfront; include “if you don’t see usage after X minutes…” troubleshooting.

Docs/Quickstart alignment reminders (Wei/Elliot)
- The checklist should be canonical; quickstarts should mirror it (same headings/order).
- Docs IA: ensure each step has exactly one “best” target page and we avoid link sprawl.
- Track parity across Python/TS/Go snippets; avoid shipping Console steps that only 1 SDK supports.

Next edits (owner: Jean-Paul)
- Tighten step names to be consistent verbs (“Create”, “Make”, “Set”, “Pin”, “Configure”, “Verify”).
- Propose final MVP step set (max 9) and mark 2 as “recommended” (streaming, observability) if needed.
- Add final deep links once Console routes are confirmed.
- Add final acceptance criteria language once PM-751 closes on TTFS/TTFP definitions.
